descriptionChirho: A vision or prophetic revelation, an Aramaic noun (חֱזוּ) used in Daniel for divinely granted visions. Appears in plural construct 'visions of the night' (arb: رُؤَى, kor: 환상들, swa: maono ya, spa: visiones de, hin: दर्शन) and singular 'in a/my vision' (arb: رُؤْيَا, kor: 환상, swa: maono, hin: दर्शन में). All translations consistently render this as prophetic vision — Arabic رُؤَى/رُؤْيَا, Korean 환상, Swahili maono, Spanish visión/visiones — confirming a unified sense of divinely mediated visual revelation in Daniel's nocturnal experiences (Dan 2:28; 4:5, 7, 10, 13; 7:1-2, 7, 13, 15).

The outward appearance or visible aspect of something, distinct from the prophetic-vision sense. In Daniel 4:11 (Aramaic), the word describes the physical look of the great tree ('and its appearance'). The multilingual evidence distinguishes this clearly: eng: 'its appearance' (not 'vision'), arb: مَنْظَرُهُ (from نظر 'to look at', not رُؤَى 'vision'), kor: 그것의 모습 ('its form/look', not 환상 'vision'), swa: sura yake ('its form/face'), spa: apariencia ('appearance'), hin: उसका रूप ('its form'). This concrete visual-descriptive sense is semantically distinct from the prophetic-revelation sense.
